input_telegraf_$measurement$_enabled.v:
[This option is just a sample. Change $measurement$ to your measurement name like $cpu$.]
Telegraf http input of the $measurement$ enabled.
$measurement$ is a variable to the measurement name of the line protocol.
eg) input_telegraf_$redis_keyspace$_enabled=true

input_telegraf_$measurement$_debug_enabl.v:
[This option is just a sample. Change $measurement$ to your measurement name like $cpu$.]
print telegraf line protocol of the $measurement$ to STDOUT

input_telegraf_$measurement$_tag_filter.v:
[This option is just a sample. Change $measurement$ to your measurement name like $cpu$.]
If set, only the metric matching to this tag value is handled.
It can have multiple values. comma separator means 'or' condition. eg) cpu:cpu-total,cpu:cpu0
It also have not(!) condition. eg) cpu:!cpu-total

input_telegraf_$measurement$_counter_map.v:
[This option is just a sample. Change $measurement$ to your measurement name like $cpu$.]
which fields of $measurement$ are mapped to scouter's counter.
format: {line-protocol field name}:{scouter counter name}:{display name?}:{unit?}:{hasTotal?}:{normalize sec?}
It can have multiple values.
 - {scouter counter name} can be defined in combination with the line protocol's tag variables.
For example, if the value of 'tag1' is 'disk01' and the value of 'tag2' is 'bin', the counter name defined as 'scouter-du-$tag1$-$tag2$' is 'scouter-du-disk01-bin'.
 eg)used_memory:tg-redis-used-memory,used_memory_rss:redis-used-memory-rss,redis used rss,bytes:true
 eg)cpu:cpu-$cpu-no$ -- this example shows counter definition with tag value.
If {line-protocol field name} is started with '&' or '&&', then It works as delta counter
When specified as a delta type, the difference in values per second is stored. and the counter name ends with '_delta'
double '&&' means BOTH type. AS BOTH type, the value and the difference value both are stored.
 - {normalize sec} applies only to a delta counter if the counter is a 'BOTH' type counter. (This value can have min 4 to max 60)

input_telegraf_$measurement$_objFamily_b.v:
[This option is just a sample. Change $measurement$ to your measurement name like $cpu$.]
define an obj Family prefix. objectType is defined with some tags.
see input_telegraf_$measurement$_objFamily_append_tags option.

input_telegraf_$measurement$_objFamily_a.v:
[This option is just a sample. Change $measurement$ to your measurement name like $cpu$.]

input_telegraf_$measurement$_objType_bas.v:
[This option is just a sample. Change $measurement$ to your measurement name like $cpu$.]

this tags's value is prepended to objType_base.
It can have multiple values. eg)tag1,tag2
